quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What happens to your steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire will make the steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should you do when someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Not worry about them and just focus on the road in front of you.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle crashes is true?

options.text: Most happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Most are caused by worn tires.
More than half involve riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders who have had less than six months of experience.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you—their headlights light the road and their taillights show if there are bumps ahead.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake on a motorcycle is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take before alcohol affects your riding?
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which riding formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to stay close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation for curves, turns, and when entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Rely only on their mirrors to identify other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Slam on the brakes to allow any vehicles in their blind spot to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which item provides the best face protection for a rider?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must finish passing without going over the speed limit.
You can finish passing in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You can go over the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must finish passing without going over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed at or below the posted speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it harder for other drivers to judge where they are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Use the brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and stay straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When securing a load, you should place the load:

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Loads should be placed low and spread evenly on both sides of the motorcycle. Placing them too high, such as on a sissy bar, raises the center of gravity and affects balance.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps your safety on the road. It helps you see and be seen better, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and prepare for turns you plan to make.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when making a turn, you should:

options.text: Always press on the left handlebar.
Always press on the right handlebar.
Press on the handlebar opposite the direction of the turn.
Press on the handlebar in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handlebar in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn a motorcycle, it must lean. To make it lean, press on the handlebar in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To lower your crash risk, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce your crash risk, make yourself as visible as possible. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely only on your mirrors to see your surroundings.
Point in the direction of the lane change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists:

options.text: Do not need space around them.
Should cut their normal space cushion in half.
Should keep enough space cushion around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should keep enough space cushion around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit how far you can see.
Let you see as far to the sides as you need.
Do not have to be worn if you think your view is limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit your vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets let you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use the safest part of the lane for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest part of the lane for current conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position based on road conditions and what is safest at that moment.

questions.question: How do you stop a motorcycle in the shortest distance?

options.text: Use both brakes without locking the wheels.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: To stop in the shortest distance on a straight road, use both brakes together. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: Several factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which does NOT affect BAC?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Where are motorcycles most likely to have conflicts with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts happen at intersections, where other vehicles may cross your path. Stay alert at all intersections.

questions.question: What should motorcycle passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Sit behind the operator and lean with them. Sit as close to the operator as comfort allows while holding their waist, hips, or belt.
